First-wave COVID mortality was concentrated in long-term care; CIHI and provincial reports document the share. CAF Operation LASER reports described conditions in assisted homes. Ownership and profit of private operators are corporate facts. Claims that MAID is designed to free LTC beds are inference unless a primary document says so.
On the record: death shares, military observations, ownership registries.
Inference (labeled): understaffing and for-profit incentives can worsen outcomes. MAID demand effects on bed census are speculative without health-system modeling from a primary agency.

When COVID-19 overwhelmed long-term care homes, the Canadian Armed Forces were deployed to assist. The military reports documented conditions that shocked the nation: residents left in soiled bedding for extended periods, cockroach and pest infestations, residents not fed or given water, aggressive behaviour by some staff, residents calling out for help with no one responding, and infection…

Research published in the Canadian Medical Association Journal found that for-profit LTC homes had higher COVID-19 death rates than non-profit and municipally operated homes. For-profit operators were more likely to have older facilities, lower staffing ratios, and fewer infection control measures. Yet for-profit operators reported continued profits during the pandemic.
